# MTRClust

`MTRClust` is an R package for robust clustering of multivariate panel
trajectories. The method estimates smooth low-rank cluster trajectories, trims
whole observations, and provides multilevel outlier diagnostics for complete
numeric panel arrays.

The main input is a numeric three-dimensional array with dimensions
`n x T x p`, where `n` is the number of units, `T` is the number of ordered time
points, and `p` is the number of variables or sensors.

## Features

* Robust clustering of complete multivariate panel arrays.
* Observation-level trimming controlled by `alpha`.
* Smooth low-rank fitted cluster trajectories.
* Explicit termination, convergence, and rollback diagnostics.
* Observation, temporal, sensor-segment, multivariate-segment, and cell-level
  diagnostic summaries.
* S3 `print()`, `summary()`, and `plot()` methods.
* A small synthetic panel-data generator.
* A helper for converting complete long-format panels to `n x T x p` arrays.

## Installation

Install the current public release from GitHub:

```r
if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("remotes")
}

remotes::install_github("hsnbulut/MTRClust")
```

Alternatively, install a downloaded source package:

```r
install.packages(
  "MTRClust_0.1.0.tar.gz",
  repos = NULL,
  type = "source"
)
```

Repository: https://github.com/hsnbulut/MTRClust

## Minimum example

```{r example}
library(MTRClust)

dat <- simulate_mtr_panel(
  n = 30,
  tt = 15,
  p = 3,
  seed = 1
)

fit <- mtrclust(
  x = dat$x,
  k = 3,
  alpha = 0.05,
  rank = 2,
  nstart = 2,
  max_iter = 20,
  seed = 1
)

print(fit)
summary(fit)
plot(fit, type = "objective")
```

This example was validated during package-release preparation. It converged
without rollback using `max_iter = 20` on the synthetic data generated above.

## Diagnostics

Summary counts and unit-level diagnostics can be obtained with:

```{r diagnostics}
mtrclust_diagnostics(fit)
head(mtrclust_diagnostics(fit, type = "units"))
```

The fitted object records the termination reason, convergence status, rollback
status, iteration count, best iteration, objective value, cluster assignments,
retained observations, fitted trajectories, and multilevel outlier diagnostics.

## Documentation

Use the package help pages and introductory vignette for the complete argument
list and interpretation guidance:

```r
?mtrclust
vignette("introduction-to-mtrclust", package = "MTRClust")
```

The package also provides `as_mtr_panel()` for converting a complete long-format
data set into the array structure required by `mtrclust()`.

## Reproducibility

`mtrclust()` uses sequential random starts by default. Set the `seed` argument
explicitly to make stochastic initialization reproducible.

The public API uses `method = "global"` by default. The legacy value
`"v6_global"` remains accepted as an alias and maps to the same validated
internal implementation.

## Research data and reproducibility

The research materials supporting the manuscript *MTRClust: Robust clustering of multivariate panel data with multilevel outlier diagnostics* (PONE-D-26-49779) are publicly available in the [research-v1.0.0 GitHub Release](https://github.com/hsnbulut/MTRClust/releases/tag/research-v1.0.0).

The research archive includes results from the 64-scenario simulation benchmark (44,800 method-result records), 9,600 ablation-fit records, 12 overlap-validation cases, and compact results from three full-data reference fits and 600 subsample fits. Analysis scripts, configurations, numerical verification tools, checksums, and reproducibility instructions are also provided.

Download the [research ZIP](https://github.com/hsnbulut/MTRClust/releases/download/research-v1.0.0/MTRClust_PONE-D-26-49779_research_v1.0.0.zip) and its [SHA256 checksum](https://github.com/hsnbulut/MTRClust/releases/download/research-v1.0.0/MTRClust_PONE-D-26-49779_research_v1.0.0.zip.sha256). Follow the README.md and REPRODUCING.md files inside the archive to verify the saved results.

The archive reconstructs stored numerical results without rerunning all historical model fits. Limitations concerning unavailable original states and some comparator assignments are documented in MISSING_DATA.md.

This research release (research-v1.0.0) is separate from the installable MTRClust R package (v0.1.0).

## Current limitations

The current implementation requires complete finite numeric arrays. Missing
values are not imputed. The default execution path is sequential.

Termination caused by reaching `max_iter` is reported separately from numerical
convergence. When rollback is enabled, a nonconverged candidate can be restored
to its best recorded objective iterate, and this action is explicitly reported
in the fitted object.

## Citation

If you use `MTRClust` in academic research, please cite the associated
methodological article:

> Bulut, H., & Osman, B. M. *MTRClust: Robust clustering of multivariate
> panel data with multilevel outlier diagnostics*. Manuscript under revision,
> PLOS ONE (PONE-D-26-49779).

Complete journal, volume, page, and article DOI information will be added after
publication. No separate software DOI is planned for this package; package users
are directed to cite the methodological article. The current package citation can
also be inspected in R:

```r
citation("MTRClust")
```

## Development status

Version `0.1.0` is the initial public release of `MTRClust`. The scientific
implementation follows the audited prototype used in the accompanying methods
manuscript.

Manuscript-scale simulations and real-data analyses are not executed by package
examples or vignettes. Their saved results and verification scripts are publicly
available in the separate research-v1.0.0 release linked above.
